**From the Team at**
**Generations for America and Generations for America Foundation**

---
Hi D. P., Generations for America Foundation is proud to announce its upcoming Spring 2026 webinar series, "The U.S. Constitution: The Shield of Rights." This twelve-week educational journey will take place every Wednesday evening from April 8 through June 24, 2026, from 7:00 - 8:00 PM EDT. This series is designed to equip Americans with a profound understanding of their fundamental rights and the individual liberties that serve as a safeguard against government overreach. Join us for any webinar or all of them. The Spring 2026 series features distinguished speakers committed to constitutional literacy. Mike Delaney: A Navy veteran with several decades of experience in engineering, Delaney applies his analytical precision to the study of constitutional frameworks. His background as a veteran and engineer brings a unique, structured perspective to understanding the historical intent and modern application of the Bill of Rights. Rocky Burke: A retired law enforcement and public safety professional with over 50 years of experience, Burke brings a career's worth of field expertise to the discussion of civic rights. His insights bridge the gap between constitutional theory and the real-world challenges facing American families today. Constitutional education from a law enforcement perspective will improve the quality of court judgments, legislation, law enforcement, voting rules and government personnel performance. It will benefit everyday Americans in terms of liberty and security.
---
| |
---
|
# Shield of Rights Constitutional Webinars
---
Know your rights and responsibilities as a resident or citizen of the USA. Special focus on law enforcement perspective is crucial for both officers and the public leading to better community relations and more informed decision-making in law enforcement. RSVP now to learn about and discuss the Constitution from the comfort of your home or convenience of your phone when on the road at [https://www.generationsforamericafoundation.com/events](http://email.robly.com/ls/click?upn=u001.P2x6L4rJRHUTLoJQXbN-2FloablzO9YKcHYYxPiBlxvKUAcpliIXPhSSftsKT4v0Lcf25Y3ja-2Bw4YO9U5UT5r-2Feg-3D-3D2oHW_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVCvXrI5zrvAmWKlzz2BTRM7s8INkI5SckbDmt-2BWdjKKGbLk6cfcI6HcTo-2FzwJlVunOo1mcou5HeXnw7GlMEdlJgkjbZCZixF-2F89PRqG-2BPYExiZ-2FFpoK11xgAkzzYy-2FGTFttFlyq1TvrdrFshUtAvX46gw1sikO9L1jkBdR-2FcWqe3ALrLMw1h3m-2B7wkn15xBey5KCDvteYl3HIijVW8eBeCbmthoxUnq39RfNB29VcO9aUL6i-2BPNJM8vWhDns8I2Olz-2FxbdxtLutbmjGcI6HDDdHmbnzlX6zbiZIXfjS6ZK5Y1vZdiCC1ZsTjtR634l4wow4YInFsP0FrGI2ZyRrrPoDtl5GYh9C3z87UbP5Kc6hfR1hraMQE-2Bxkv2L77xOyG-2B1W9yVIBqPzQeqElGKXWgmTSoJklpRVqiWA35PcW4TNoxbQ3DldglYiIoYQifXgnLhvm3TpSDBge1-2F6kPHoHY3cwwCbJACO6EAHOwk1HUh03NVBuVwZ81VN0-2FQGsgctNfk6gzD4xdVsBEtkoykF4XZgCNEfJ-2Fjrks4tMxNokPA1-2BA-3D-3D)

# Robert's Rules of Order
---

P., Generations for America Foundation is proud to announce its upcoming Spring 2026 webinar series, "The U.S. Constitution: The Shield of Rights." This twelve-week educational journey will take place every Wednesday evening from April 8 through June 24, 2026, from 7:00 - 8:00 PM EDT. This series is designed to equip Americans with a profound understanding of their fundamental rights and the individual liberties that serve as a safeguard against government overreach. Join us for any webinar or all of them. The Spring 2026 series features distinguished speakers committed to constitutional literacy. Mike Delaney: A Navy veteran with several decades of experience in engineering, Delaney applies his analytical precision to the study of constitutional frameworks. His background as a veteran and engineer brings a unique, structured perspective to understanding the historical intent and modern application of the Bill of Rights. Rocky Burke: A retired law enforcement and public safety professional with over 50 years of experience, Burke brings a career's worth of field expertise to the discussion of civic rights. His insights bridge the gap between constitutional theory and the real-world challenges facing American families today. Constitutional education from a law enforcement perspective will improve the quality of court judgments, legislation, law enforcement, voting rules and government personnel performance. 314 Action has helped elect hundreds of Democratic scientists across the country, flipping critical seats and building a movement rooted in facts, evidence, and real problem-solving.
And now, they’re backing our campaign.
But this endorsement isn’t just about me. It’s about something bigger — a growing movement to bring science, truth, and integrity back into government.
Because right now, we’re seeing exactly what happens when science is pushed aside:
❌ Public health decisions driven by politics instead of evidence
❌ Attacks on vaccines and basic medical facts
❌ Chaos inside the very agencies meant to protect us
314 Action exists to fight back against that — by electing leaders who will follow the data, trust experts, and put people over politics.
That’s the kind of leadership I’ve tried to bring in Georgia. And now, with this endorsement, we have the chance to take that fight to Congress.
But here’s the truth: Endorsements don’t win elections — people do.
Grassroots support is what allows campaigns like ours to compete, organize, and win tough races against well-funded opponents. So I’m asking: Can you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can today to help us build on this momentum and show that this pro-science movement is strong in Georgia? Joining me is Author, speaker and former Sheriff Richard Mack who has served in a wide variety of roles over the course of his nearly twenty year career in law enforcement, which began in Provo, Utah. After 11 years at Provo PD, Mack decided to return to his childhood turf in Arizona and run for Graham County Sheriff. His campaign took off and he was elected in 1988.
During his tenure, federal officers informed the sheriffs of the state that they would be required to enforce the so-called "Brady Bill" and run background checks at their expense under the law. In 1994, Mack and six other sheriffs from across the country, challenged the constitutionality of the Brady Bill and ultimately, fought it all the way to the United States Supreme Court, where they won a monumental decision for freedom. Three years later, in a landmark 5-4 split decision based on the Tenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, Mack won his case.
He has also been named Elected Official of the Year by the Arizona-New Mexico Coalition of Counties in 1994, received the NRA Law Officer of the Year, inducted into the NRA Hall of Fame, 1995 Cicero Award, Samuel Adams Leadership Award from the Local Sovereignty Coalition, and Gun Owners of America Defender of the Second Amendment Award. He was sheriff for two terms until 1997. Sheriff Mack currently teaches, consults and empowers people around the country and around the world. He started the Constitutional Sheriffs & Peace Officers Association (CSPOA) which educates both citizens as well as sheriffs and other peace officers on the Constitution and their limitations of power, according to the Constitution. For more about Sheriff Richard Mack visit [https://cspoa.org/about/sheriff-mack/](https://substack.com/redirect/97707d20-f966-42fc-984a-4c319bc90962?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

After 11 years at Provo PD, Mack decided to return to his childhood turf in Arizona and run for Graham County Sheriff. His campaign took off and he was elected in 1988. During his tenure, federal officers informed the sheriffs of the state that they would be required to enforce the so-called "Brady Bill" and run background checks at their expense under the law. In 1994, Mack and six other sheriffs from across the country, challenged the constitutionality of the Brady Bill and ultimately, fought it all the way to the United States Supreme Court, where they won a monumental decision for freedom. Three years later, in a landmark 5-4 split decision based on the Tenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, Mack won his case. He has also been named Elected Official of the Year by the Arizona-New Mexico Coalition of Counties in 1994, received the NRA Law Officer of the Year, inducted into the NRA Hall of Fame, 1995 Cicero Award, Samuel Adams Leadership Award from the Local Sovereignty Coalition, and Gun Owners of America Defender of the Second Amendment Award. He was sheriff for two terms until 1997. Sheriff Mack currently teaches, consults and empowers people around the country and around the world. He started the Constitutional Sheriffs & Peace Officers Association (CSPOA) which educates both citizens as well as sheriffs and other peace officers on the Constitution and their limitations of power, according to the Constitution. Peter.

recent polling.

First, the good stuff: we’re leading in favorability in one poll. In
another, we take the lead once voters hear about what our campaign is
fighting for.

Those are both great signals that we’re in a strong position to win this
primary.

Now, the caveat: the other candidates know this too, and they’re already
trying to stop us.

In the past week or so, the corporate-backed establishment has launched
coordinated attacks against our campaign in an effort to curb our
momentum.

While their first few hits failed to land, there’s no telling what could
come next — and
Peter, they have some powerful
forces waiting in the wings, including corporate PACs with nearly endless
amounts of money.

Here’s the part I need you to remember: polling doesn’t win elections.
Resources do.

If we have the resources to reach people — to explain why it shouldn’t be
this hard to afford healthcare, to pay the bills, to trust that government
works for you — then we win.

If we don’t, they will spend whatever it takes to define us before we can
define ourselves.

But my story of grit and service proves I'm ready to fight. | Raised in North Georgia's mountains as a ninth-generation local, I've dedicated my life to strong communities and thriving Main Streets. I captained Emory's basketball team, earned degrees from Emory and Cornell, and was an All-State high school star averaging 18 points. At 31, thyroid cancer hit me hard. After a 13-hour surgery and ICU stay, I defied doctors with 10 post-op pushups. The cancer is gone, and I’m still here. It was at this moment I knew God had given me more time for a reason. | Patriot, I'll be honest with you. I've been watching the debate over the SAVE America Act in Washington — and while I'm cheering for it to pass, I've been in this fight long enough to know something most people won't say: **We cannot afford to wait on Washington to save our elections.** While politicians debate, the Democrat ground game does not stop. Their voter registration staffers are at their tables right now. Their ballot chasers are making their calls. Their door knockers are hitting their lists. _And if we are not doing the same thing — right now — we are falling behind._ **I know this because I've lived it.** In 2024, my team spent over a year embedded on the ground in Pennsylvania before Election Day. We helped register hundreds of thousands of new Republican voters. We chased down every outstanding mail-in ballot we legally could. We drove voters to the polls on Election Day. **That is why Pennsylvania went red.** Not because of any law. Not because of any court ruling. Because of boots on the ground, day after day, doing the unglamorous, exhausting, absolutely essential work of grassroots organizing.

Will you chip in to my campaign today in honor of him and all the good people out there fighting? [] CHIP IN [] Thank you, Marlene [] About Marlene Galan-Woods Marlene Galán-Woods is a former broadcast journalist and mother of five who has lived in Arizona for the past 36 years. Her parents fled communist Cuba looking for a better life. Their risk paid off and allowed Marlene to pursue her career as a broadcast journalist which brought her to Arizona. She met the love of her life, Grant Woods, and they raised a family together before he passed away in 2021. Marlene is running for Congress to stand up to extremists and be a voice for all Arizonans. And here's why:
From unaffordable housing to inaccessible health care and struggling schools, Colorado faces real problems. But I know solutions are within our reach.
I've spent years working to deliver change for Colorado from the U.S. Senate. And after traveling to every corner of our state, building relationships and convening Coloradans of all stripes to take on our greatest challenges, together, we've succeeded – by passing the Affordable Care Act, expanding the Child Tax Credit, investing in high-speed internet, upgrading our roads and bridges, and capping prescription drug costs for seniors.
But given Trump's thirst for power and the cowardly partisanship that's infected his party, it's clear that the best solutions to our problems _will not_ come from the broken politics or Trump’s chaos in D.C. They have to start here in Colorado. **And that's why I'm running.**
I'm running for governor to rebuild our middle class and to build an economy that works for everyone, not just the people at the top.
I'm running to ensure we set the nationwide example of how to really protect working families from Trump's costly tariffs and cruel agenda.
**I'm running because I know that together, we can create lasting solutions to our shared challenges, and make Colorado the best place to live and raise a family – but to make that happen, I need you with me.**

body:
Let’s look at how many he’s broken:

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128986839/612916715/-1080040549?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMTkyNjI5Mi1hYzMyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qDlspr3br7Tn6qSxCLnHEP3ASAS1stOWNvRvBp_3p3Y=) Trump has made a lot of promises to the American people and broken most of them. He “promised” to restore law and order — in reality, his administration is weaponizing the federal government against American citizens. name: Wes Moore
subject: Who’s paying for this reckless war
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1260%2E1086043%2EO2bpp0)
Peter,
As Trump’s war of choice goes on, everyday Americans are paying the price.
Energy costs and gas prices are rising day by day. And now, Trump’s proposing to pay for his reckless war by taking away people’s health care. Their latest request would cut funding on everything from roads to hospitals to pay for an even more out-of-control defense budget.
**It’s nonsense, and it’s not what any of us want.**
This White House is making these decisions without partnering with the states. We’re doing what we can for the people of Maryland, but we have to be clear -- the federal government has gone all-in on this reckless war of choice and decided to stop doing its job.
While we’re in the legislative session I’m working with the Maryland House and Senate on proposals to cut utility costs and bring relief to Marylanders. **[You can read the latest on our work to bring down costs here.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/1341?t=2&akid=1260%2E1086043%2EO2bpp0)**
Elevate,
Wes

clean_body: Trump’s “it’s too hard, let’s just not do it” attitude is exactly why I’m running for Congress. We can’t let extremists who put themselves above your family continue to call the shots. | = | Peter, Donald Trump just said we can’t afford to take care of things like childcare, Medicaid, and Medicare – because apparently, “we’re fighting wars” and “it’s not possible.” 🙄 Well, I’ve got news for him: The American people deserve better than excuses! Childcare is essential for working families. Medicaid and Medicare are lifelines for millions of people across this country. And we CAN afford them – we must prioritize people over corporate profits and political games. Trump’s “it’s too hard, let’s just not do it” attitude is exactly why I’m running for Congress. We can’t let extremists who put themselves above your family continue to call the shots. That’s why I’m fighting for affordable childcare, for accessible healthcare, and for a government that actually serves the people, not the rich and powerful. = | | | = | = | = | = | = Trump can try to talk his way out of it, but we know that a country that doesn’t care for its own people will never be great. Let’s show him how wrong he is. Michigan is the single most important Senate race on the map this year.
And the Republicans confirmed it.
**Senate Leadership Fund, the largest GOP super PAC, just announced they’re dropping** _**$45 million**_**into Michigan to try and buy this open seat.**
To put that in perspective, that’s more than they’re spending in Georgia, Maine, Alaska, Iowa, _and_ New Hampshire. Because they know — if they can buy Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat, they block the Democrats from having _any_ chance at flipping control of the U.S. Senate to serve as a real check on Trump. It’s a massive amount of money aimed directly at defeating _**us**_. _They think they can buy this seat._

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

With the SAVE Act, the Trump administration is trying to make it harder for millions of Americans to vote. Here’s the thing: You don’t have to take our word about how bad this legislation would be, Peter — just take a look at Kansas. Lawmakers there passed a similar law 15 years ago, and chaos ensued. **At least 31,000 people were prevented from registering to vote.** This created a ripple effect in the state’s critical gubernatorial election — incumbent Republican Governor Sam Brownback defeated Democrat Paul Davis by the thinnest of margins. **We’re approaching one of the most consequential midterm elections in recent memory this November. **[As Drought Deepens, Colorado Still Has No Rules For Data Center Water Use](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
In Aurora, data center proposals run through a simple filter. City officials compare total water use against how much of that water won’t come back—lost to evaporation. If either number gets too high, the project doesn’t move forward.
When a developer wants to build in Denver, there is no matrix.
That gap—two cities, two standards, nothing statewide connecting them—is the center of a question Colorado has avoided answering: who is responsible for knowing how much water AI data centers use, and when does that become too much?
The question got harder to ignore this spring. On March 16, Governor Jared Polis activated Phase 2 of the state’s Drought Response Plan—the first activation in nearly six years—after federal water managers ranked this year’s snowpack 45th out of 46 years on record.

**[El Paso Co. found a way to cut undeliverable ballots and clean voter rolls—Colorado leaders looked away](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY BOB COOPER, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Costly inefficiencies in voter rolls highlighted:** Colorado processed over 323,000 undeliverable ballots in 2024—costing an estimated $1.6 million—due to outdated voter registration data and limitations in current systems.
* **El Paso County pilot shows measurable improvements:** Using credit agency data, the county identified over 91,000 address discrepancies, corrected thousands of records, and saved about $107,000, demonstrating a potential “best practice” for improving accuracy.
* **Statewide solution proposed but not adopted:** A $50,000 plan to expand the system statewide and reduce costs was not implemented after legislation stalled and state officials declined to act, leaving the current system unchanged.

* **Debate centers on verification vs. authority:** Colorado officials say the state’s voter rolls are continuously maintained using multiple data sources, while critics argue the system lacks independent auditing to verify accuracy.
* **Federal order sparks legal and constitutional clash:** Colorado joined a multistate lawsuit challenging a federal voter verification order, with officials arguing election authority belongs to states and Congress—not the executive branch.
* **Discrepancies and transparency concerns highlighted:** Critics point to issues like address mismatches, undeliverable ballots, and limited access to federal citizenship data as evidence of gaps, while supporters maintain the current system is well-managed despite imperfections.

**[Colorado’s ‘politically homeless’ voters: Who’s showing up—and who’s not](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**

Last week we finished 81 days in Boise.
And I want to give you the real account of what happened, not the version that makes everyone look good.
So, _a few_ wins first.
I personally carried the bill that stripped teachers' union dues off the taxpayer dime. Got it passed (waiting ont he Governor to sign it... still). American law for American courts (I pushed that through in the Senate) is now signed into law. And my voter affidavit reform that actually puts teeth into ID voter verification at the polls is now law. These weren't wins that fell into my lap. I put my name on the legislation and dragged them through to the finish line.
We also landed some hits on the money side. Idaho's sitting on a $1.6 billion surplus and the instinct in that building was to spend it. Every surplus is an invitation to grow government, and there are plenty of people in Boise who answered that invitation enthusiastically.
I didn't.
We pushed through rescissions and budget cuts that clawed back agency spending (and gutted millions from the fed-funded Minnesota-style daycare program too). But I want to be straight with you about what all of this actually is. Cutting agencies and clawing back program dollars is treating symptoms.
_**The disease is a spending culture in Boise that assumes every surplus belongs to the government first.**_
I held the line where I could but I'm not in the majority the way I'd need to be to actually win that war. So we won some battles this session. But the war is still very much going. And nothing proves that more than the biggest fight we could have had this session, _the one we didn 't have_. Not really, anyway. I'm talking about illegal immigration. It's not just a "federal issue." It touches everyone in Idaho. Your neighbor who can't find construction work. The school that can't figure out who's actually enrolled. The wage that won't go up because someone will always undercut it with labor that doesn't cost what labor should cost.
I personally went in with several enforcement bills and they ALL got killed or refused a hearing before most Idahoans ever heard they existed.
Not by Democrats. _But by our own Republican supermajority._
That's where we're at as a state. And you know what I keep coming back to? Somebody profits from this. Somebody profits when enforcement is weak and workers are cheap and nobody asks questions. And those somebodies were in that building, quiet and patient and effective, the whole session.
The Idaho Sheriff's Association showed up to help kill the ICE cooperation bill I co-sponsored (and there were several more bills they testified AGAINST). I saw committee chairmen make bills disappear into their desks. And I watched every single bill we had die or got no hearing. Yes, in "Republican Idaho." So while most legislators from safe Republican districts will send you an end-of-session letter that lists all the wins and call it a day...
_**I 'm not going to do that.**_
Because you deserve to know what the cheap labor lobby still has on the Idaho statehouse. Their stranglehold didn't loosen this session (if anything, now I know exactly how tight it is).
What you get from having me in that building is simple.
Someone who names it. Someone whose name is actually on the enforcement bills (not just the press releases). And someone who isn't going to tell you we had a "great session" when the most important lever we had didn't get pulled.
That's the report from Boise.
Most people in Idaho have no idea any of this happened. You do now. That matters more than you think.

**Born and raised in the Twin Cities, Royce White was the son of a single mother and started playing sports at the age of 5 years old. Living in various neighborhoods growing up, much of his family remained in the Rondo community, where he spent much of his time and received schooling. White excelled at basketball and recieved a scholarship to play basketball at the University of Minnesota, and later transferred to Iowa State. In 20 years of service I never once heard language like that from anyone in a position of authority over the American military force. body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128991150/612928941/-975735282?refcode=em_logoheader&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOTg5MGNjMy1iNjMyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TIpSiVkqxmkFM3aYd5NJ_RXriqOt8kWfcoMPt8INzk8=)

Peter,

Today we celebrate World Health Day, and here's something I and everyone who has ever personally suffered or had a family member who struggles with the healthcare system know about health: **It's fragile.**

It's something you don't always think about until it changes, and when it does, everything in your life spirals. Your routines, your finances, your sense of stability, even your future. It can all shift at a moment's notice.

I know that because when I was younger, my dad got sick. He couldn’t work, and we lost our health insurance. What followed was one of the hardest chapters of my life. My family was constantly forced to choose between paying bills and affording my dad's care. Every decision felt impossible, and over time, we lost so much trying to keep up. This time in my life showed me, in a way nothing else could, just how important accessible, affordable healthcare really is.

I want to make sure no family is thrown off a cliff like mine was. I believe government can help build a system where people get the care they need without risking everything they've worked for — where families can focus on healing instead of bills and where communities can truly thrive.

But right now, we're moving in the wrong direction.

Mariannette Miller-Meeks has voted to cut Medicaid and weaken rural hospitals that communities depend on. She stood by as SNAP benefits were reduced, taking food away from families who are already struggling. She allowed the Affordable Care Act tax credits that so many Iowa families rely on to expire, making coverage harder to afford.

She has consistently supported anti-abortion legislation and cheered on the _Dobbs_ decision that overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , paving the way for Iowa's near-total abortion ban. And here in our district, we've already seen multiple health centers close their labor and delivery services because of budget cuts.

This is not a record anyone should be proud to run on. **I'm running to build something different – to make sure families don't have to live with the kind of fear mine did and to protect the care that so many people rely on every day.**

**[If we're going to bring true, lasting change to our district, we all need to be in this together. That starts with chipping in to my campaign to ensure we have the resources to defeat Miller-Meeks this November. If you're ready to put an end to these attacks on our healthcare, support our movement today>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128991151/612928949/-2009658230?refcode=em26_260407_WHD_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260407_WHD_fnd_gq_act___CB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=29890cc3-b632-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOTg5MGNjMy1iNjMyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TIpSiVkqxmkFM3aYd5NJ_RXriqOt8kWfcoMPt8INzk8=)**

Christina

Radical Democrats just surged in Minnesota. National extremists are pouring in millions to flip our state. | [](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=87b211c3861e46e3812d2945271c80a6&_e=3d6mDXK-5LVw1Xl3lLDEZHP4cW7g4gL5otvqCC0ymOiy-PlTP-bF0C_C-M4qaPixUu0jZYjQesCcXSdE-2r0A31tLOMuwZrImZqODiUUSwU-RdawUgByMg_ui8-mSGf8mlTA8lK1YX3ybripeK3HZmh1PxNSTCbBJS_5vYKC2FpLlBeBZo3WpT9nPOdqTJTIumwqr4PSbqFWptnvchQ_LMrVfSVSnQxAs3O1_CuxsAzOMxSu_WR5ZTfB2BiiGHblZNalmUOKA20D3k1S-WACKioSLnUXdL-sZeMy6QG03jwLVjS26MW-F2gQhKcPAH0hdixTEYbVnnXWmzUwkEgmOGWIqRb_mGimqvl4TASmF1oJ9pXd39mf1-X_osVYGELZ_aPHYlN3j6OCWLKxwNMu0GpbpLikfXO3V5xhrV1yidBdX12Dd1ZvbX9gHVLsc15I0Y_z91b91c_wq1YsWViIdoqCMPM7l5nbN8WKBZcLqmoQEsVNmNCJonDqPQ2f9wkN_rcUEW__PwdCTMQE8L6tO7C9_DNISdkmpbaGIAcc0z4lHNwtP-aqDvq6euuK6FFSghU0xrC5kcwFK4yOWK3d7tJOH1eqJepzNOlm9FSJxQNpNURKnBMrRPL8J-Po7tI5Rw3o-3wFJm8cGEM8GBfKCSwBnP7LjLjKSV64upnj2XDyGparlFfLQTrjIMa0_k8dt8NWpq7c31e-mn56zPhM7HIv1RuKit7nviEmX5NucV0j2SDkDEeXYA8SzMPpUTbg)

---
Fellow Conservative,

As we approach the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, I’ve been thinking a lot about the courage of our Founding Fathers.

250 years ago, 56 patriots risked everything — their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor — to create the greatest country the world has ever seen. A nation founded on liberty, opportunity, and the God-given rights we still cherish today.

That same spirit of patriotism is what called me to service. **On my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after 9/11, I joined the Marine Corps and later became a Navy SEAL.** I deployed nine times to over 70 countries, risking my life to defend the Constitution and the American way of life my parents taught me to love.

Today, as a proud Minnesotan running for the U.S. Senate, I’m fighting to protect that same legacy. But while Republicans continue standing for the core values that built Minnesota and America — strong families, secure borders, safe streets, free enterprise, and real opportunity — _**the Democratic Party has been overtaken by something completely unrecognizable.**_
**_
Just take a look at the photo below: _**

_[](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=87b211c3861e46e3812d2945271c80a6&_e=3d6mDXK-5LVw1Xl3lLDEZHP4cW7g4gL5otvqCC0ymOiy-PlTP-bF0C_C-M4qaPixUu0jZYjQesCcXSdE-2r0A31tLOMuwZrImZqODiUUSwU-RdawUgByMg_ui8-mSGf8mlTA8lK1YX3ybripeK3HZmh1PxNSTCbBJS_5vYKC2FpLlBeBZo3WpT9nPOdqTJTIumwqr4PSbqFWptnvchQ_LMrVfSVSnQxAs3O1_CuxsAzOMxSu_WR5ZTfB2BiiGHblZNalmUOKA20D3k1S-WACKgFaOFmD7EUXpGPD5RxfY0wQlKTx5EuYx6W3VySjxXbFlsG-n0xgH_634FYIFeFR1LfjViYhtEZDlJVLDvEbekgao4WP6uA0TIfEC1CNKHboDhiq-OcDtIAlrGKbpeYLcjUctgnEQ8lnWmrD6slBRNyIRl8WcZhZK-s1H6s0BmIaPe7RK-OOyWcDjDV12aDrkQCK_833f31Ca-1fBEYRRI9MScbGABcRbmgtlPlFMQhdZMLdG1xjiq0Co-5bHBy-mqCUUeJ3mJJdD2MvzXDcUVu8VazsfC-jZ-79T5we6gSe_2eKSEHLHRtQeb3hiLbyeBr8Zps7t28iv4cmP9rfPUNggKzanBppJFRVIL_Hb5LxuguL3cppH_sUN-Gc0PkZef3TPmevNTN1uzJQRxpxw4YhFwnXNSC2VOP_bdGEl4yBle6fASkEITbKUV3_X8Qa2dpascry18VmWbc_QmmACyV6qYpcCILAdVU3OmmESxsh)_
This is Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan, she’s my main opponent in this race. You can see here she is cosplaying as a Somali Muslim. It smells exactly like another Elizabeth Warren — cultural appropriation at its most cynical, and we don’t need another radical like that representing Minnesota in the United States Senate.

That is not the Minnesota I grew up in — playing hockey in a working-class family and learning to love this country. **It’s not the America I risked my life to defend across nine deployments. And it’s not the future any of us want for our children as we head toward America’s 250th birthday.**

My name is Adam Schwarze. I’m not a career politician. subject: I apologize for asking again
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
Not what I spent my time doing

| | | | |
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. I couldn't just sit there.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDQwN19QOS1SRC4xMTAxMTdfdDE4NjQ4NzktMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA0MDdfUDktUkQuMTEwMTE3X3QxODY0ODc5LTIwNjgifQ/KD4MGFPAkVyNBq-e8KDbIA)
But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don’t have a massive machine behind me. I don’t have someone who can write blank checks on a whim.
[I just have normal folks like you.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDQwN19QOS1SRC4xMTAxMTdfdDE4NjQ4NzktMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA0MDdfUDktUkQuMTEwMTE3X3QxODY0ODc5LTIwNjgifQ/TYQ7f_ZB2LAxGHFr4KSArg)

A MaineCare provider at the center of a widening political and financial scandal is alleged to have over-billed taxpayers by more than $1.6 million -- but repaid only a fraction of that amount, according to newly obtained state records.
Financial data produced by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) in response to a Freedom of Access Act request show that Gateway Community Services repaid just **$118,431.58** to the state through a series of Medicaid recoupments, despite state claims that the organization improperly billed at least $1.6 million over the last decade.
After ignoring _The Robinson Reports ' _coverage of Gateway Community Services for a decade, the Mills Administration finally admitted that Gateway had over-billed taxpayers by $1,068,598 between March 2021 and December 2022, and an additional $662,608 between 2015 and 2018.
The discrepancy -- roughly seven cents repaid for every dollar allegedly over-billed -- comes as a former insider has accused Gateway of systematically exploiting Maine's Medicaid system for years.
That means the three DHHS audits that cumulatively estimated Gateway Community Services' improper payments at $1.6 million may be a radical underestimate of the true amount of money that flowed to Gateway for services never rendered.

Christopher Bernardini, a former Gateway employee whose allegations have been cited in prior _Robinson Report_ and _Maine Wire_ coverage, has claimed that Gateway engaged in systematic Medicaid fraud for more than five year**s** , raising questions about both the scale of improper billing and the adequacy of state oversight.
Bernardini brought these allegations to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) during the Biden Administration and to the Office of State Auditor Matt Dunlap in 2024 -- almost a year before he spoke with media about the allegations.
Yet Bernardini received no response from either government agency.
Instead, when he publicly spoke about the manipulation of billing records and the falsification of Medicaid claims he allegedly witnessed, Maine Revenue Services audited his taxes.
The DHHS records show that Gateway's repayments were not sporadic, but highly structured -- at least originally.

Throughout 2019, the organization made repeated repayments -- most in the exact amount of $10,416.82 -- on a near-monthly basis. That pattern suggests a formal recoupment agreement or audit-driven repayment schedule rather than isolated billing corrections. That agreement would have been put in place under Republican Gov. Paul LePage, as the payments began before Gov. Janet Mills (D) was sworn in.
A smaller adjustment appears at the end of that year, followed by a multi-year gap. In 2020, all recoupment payments came to a halt.
Repayments then resumed in 2025 -- roughly four months after the _Robinson Report_ first reported on Bernardini's allegations -- with five separate transactions of $2,841.28 between August and December.
Altogether, the repayments total just over $118,000; however, the records provided by DHHS may not cover payments made between now and when the FOAA request was submitted.
The records do not show any repayment approaching the full $1.6 million that state officials have indicated was improperly billed. The small amount of recoupment is even more glaring in light of Bernardini's allegations that Gateway falsely inflated MaineCare claims over a period of more than five years.
He has claimed that Gateway's practices were not accidental errors, but part of a deliberate and sustained scheme to maximize Medicaid reimbursements -- particularly within MaineCare-funded residential and behavioral health programs.
Those claims align with broader concerns about Maine's Medicaid system, particularly under Section 21 waiver programs, where providers receive significant public funding to serve individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
The financial questions surrounding Gateway are compounded by its receipt of no-bid government contracts from the Mills Administration. Shortly after the migrant agency stopped making recoupment payments to DHHS, the agency began receiving Covid-19 Era payments (funded through federal grants) to engage in public health work. That work amounted to sending Gateway staffers into migrant neighborhoods to sign residents up for Medicaid and other welfare programs.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/975e5d5e-4ea9-4035-baa0-26ede8f4b7a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |

Around the same time that Gateway began receiving no-bid contract dollars from the Mills Administration, Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland) also began reporting on her financial disclosures that she was an "Assistant Executive Director" at Gateway Community Services.
The Gateway case became the first public test of Maine's ability -- and willingness -- to police its Medicaid system amid a nationwide reckoning over systemic fraud within the trillion-dollar welfare program.

Although DHHS had audited Gateway on three separate occasions and found over-billing issues, the Mills Administration had always kept the results of those audits private and never moved to cut off Medicaid payments to the agency.
Only 10 months after the _Robinson Report_ published the whistleblower allegations against the company, and national media began to re-report Bernardini's claims and DHHS audit documents, did the Mills Administration cut off funding for Gateway.
As a lame duck governor who is also seeking the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination in Maine, Mills has downplayed reports of fraud within MaineCare. This includes the federal audit released by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid (CMS), which revealed $46 million in overpayments within the child autism program in just one year, 2023.
Yet even as she downplays reports of MaineCare fraud, the governor has quietly moved to freeze new provider enrollment in four of the largest and most expensive MaineCare programs -- an indication that Mills may be saying one thing for political purposes while rapidly trying to resolve a crisis she can no longer contain.

“Wiping out an entire civilization is the definition of genocide. Any order given to that effect must be refused by every service member up and down the chain — period.
“This is exactly what senators were talking about when they issued a video saying illegal orders must be refused. Now it may be time for service members to follow their recommendation.”
Such an operation would put the lives of American service members and the integrity of American armed forces in jeopardy. Trump cannot be allowed to carry out this threat.
The Team at VoteVets

_" You may all go to hell, and I will go to Texas."_
When Davy Crockett uttered these words in 1835 after losing his congressional reelection bid, the Tennessee legend wasn't retreating--he was advancing toward the Alamo. Today, that same spirit animates the most consequential political battle in America, not in Washington, but in Austin.

The federal system is broken. With $40 trillion in debt, a Senate parliamentarian gutting reconciliation, and DOGE shown the door, D.C. has become a $40 trillion graveyard of conservative ambition. While Ken Paxton prepares to leave Texas for what will surely disillusion him in the Senate, others are heading the opposite direction. Chip Roy, the fifth-generation Texan with Alamo blood in his veins, is running for Attorney General--a move that represents something rare in modern politics: a recognition that the real fight has moved to the states.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.wpu1ThXLpxqnEmYGHWl9fVpT7CjUZO_AAUn_-mWQJzA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=193498890)

Texas is the largest conservative state in the union, and its AG will become the primary bulwark against federal overreach. Roy represents the "go to hell, I'm going to Texas" ethos Crockett embodied--swearing an oath to both constitutions while preparing to defend the Lone Star State against Washington's encroachment. This matters because the storm is coming.

The "three I's" of 2016--Inflation, Immigration, and Islam--remain unresolved. Despite Trump's tenure, these issues lacked lasting policy fixes. Meanwhile, the left's judicial infrastructure remains intact, with Obama-Soros appointees serving lifetime tenements, ensuring "No Kings" applies only to conservative governance. The exodus of conservative fighters tells the tale: DeSantis is termed out, Thomas Massie faces defeat, Marjorie Taylor Greene quit, Mark Green resigned, and even stalwarts like Marsha Blackburn and Tommy Tuberville are fleeing to their home states, realizing the swamp cannot be drained from within.

The warning signs are flashing red. Republicans have hemorrhaged special elections, including Trump's own Mar-a-Lago district. Virginia and North Carolina have fallen--Youngkin's legacy erased in a month, constitutional norms dismantled, with Washington State's illegal income tax providing the blueprint for national overreach. Imagine Jamie Raskin as Attorney General, AOC at HHS, or Jasmine Crockett defining housing policy for billions of dollars. This isn't fear-mongering; it's Tuesday if the pendulum swings.

By 2030, Census data counting illegal immigrants will manufacture congressional seats in Michigan and Louisiana with phantom constituents. Another flood of ten million illegals threatens to overwhelm the finger-in-the-dike enforcement Trump and Tom Homan managed.

Crockett died at the Alamo, but his choice--to fight where the battle mattered most rather than plead with a broken system--echoes through history. Chip Roy represents that same calculation. When the federal government has failed, when the fighters have departed, when the spending cannot stop and the debt cannot be contained, the states become the last redoubt. Texas isn't just a state; it's the Alamo of American conservatism. And in 2025, as in 1835, the real heroes aren't heading to Washington--they're going home to defend it.

When Washington starts sinking, apparently the escape plan comes with boots, barbecue, and a Texas flag. | | | Apr 7 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- " You may all go to hell, and I will go to Texas." When Davy Crockett uttered these words in 1835 after losing his congressional reelection bid, the Tennessee legend wasn't retreating--he was advancing toward the Alamo. Today, that same spirit animates the most consequential political battle in America, not in Washington, but in Austin. The federal system is broken. With $40 trillion in debt, a Senate parliamentarian gutting reconciliation, and DOGE shown the door, D.C. has become a $40 trillion graveyard of conservative ambition. While Ken Paxton prepares to leave Texas for what will surely disillusion him in the Senate, others are heading the opposite direction. Chip Roy, the fifth-generation Texan with Alamo blood in his veins, is running for Attorney General--a move that represents something rare in modern politics: a recognition that the real fight has moved to the states. Texas is the largest conservative state in the union, and its AG will become the primary bulwark against federal overreach. Roy represents the "go to hell, I'm going to Texas" ethos Crockett embodied--swearing an oath to both constitutions while preparing to defend the Lone Star State against Washington's encroachment. This matters because the storm is coming. The "three I's" of 2016--Inflation, Immigration, and Islam--remain unresolved. Despite Trump's tenure, these issues lacked lasting policy fixes. Meanwhile, the left's judicial infrastructure remains intact, with Obama-Soros appointees serving lifetime tenements, ensuring "No Kings" applies only to conservative governance. The exodus of conservative fighters tells the tale: DeSantis is termed out, Thomas Massie faces defeat, Marjorie Taylor Greene quit, Mark Green resigned, and even stalwarts like Marsha Blackburn and Tommy Tuberville are fleeing to their home states, realizing the swamp cannot be drained from within. The warning signs are flashing red. Republicans have hemorrhaged special elections, including Trump's own Mar-a-Lago district. Virginia and North Carolina have fallen--Youngkin's legacy erased in a month, constitutional norms dismantled, with Washington State's illegal income tax providing the blueprint for national overreach. Imagine Jamie Raskin as Attorney General, AOC at HHS, or Jasmine Crockett defining housing policy for billions of dollars. This isn't fear-mongering; it's Tuesday if the pendulum swings. By 2030, Census data counting illegal immigrants will manufacture congressional seats in Michigan and Louisiana with phantom constituents. Another flood of ten million illegals threatens to overwhelm the finger-in-the-dike enforcement Trump and Tom Homan managed. Crockett died at the Alamo, but his choice--to fight where the battle mattered most rather than plead with a broken system--echoes through history. Chip Roy represents that same calculation. When the federal government has failed, when the fighters have departed, when the spending cannot stop and the debt cannot be contained, the states become the last redoubt. Texas isn't just a state; it's the Alamo of American conservatism. And in 2025, as in 1835, the real heroes aren't heading to Washington--they're going home to defend it. We’re now hearing reports that President Donald Trump is considering an executive order declaring a so-called “emergency” to seize greater federal authority over elections.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260407em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260407em]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260407em]
This is deeply alarming to say the least.
But you don’t have to take my word for it: Our founders were explicit about this. They had just fought a king. They understood that concentrating too much power in one person was dangerous. That’s why the Constitution divides authority and states administer elections.
That’s why no president — no matter how loud or how desperate — gets to override the system because he’s afraid of losing.
As Oregon’s Secretary of State, I oversee our elections. I take an oath to the Constitution — not to any president. And I will stand up to any administration that tries to abuse emergency powers to interfere with Oregon’s voting systems or intimidate our election workers.
But I need your help to keep up the fight in light of Trump’s illegal actions, which is why I’m reaching out today. Can I count on you to join me in this fight against President Trump’s lawlessness by chipping in $5, $10, or more right away? Communicating this threat to Oregonians statewide requires resources. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260407em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260407em]
We’ve already beaten back federal overreach in court before. When attempts were made to stretch authority beyond its limits, Oregon pushed back — and won.
If we have to do it again, we will.
But defending democracy requires a strong grassroots team prepared to meet the fight head-on — and that’s where you come in.
If you believe, as I do, that no president should be able to manufacture an emergency to grab control over elections, I’m asking you to stand with me. Please contribute today to help us protect Oregon’s elections and hold President Trump accountable before it’s too late. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260407em]
Thank you,
Tobias Read

Before Trump ever uttered the phrase "Project 2025" \- the policies that would soon be forced upon the nation were tested here in Louisiana years before.
The state of Louisiana is MAGA's laboratory for testing their most depraved, cruel, and immoral policies and we the people of Louisianan are their guinea pigs.
Now a new slate of even darker policies are being tested here:

ICE roundups with unprecedented brutality. Black sites where migrants disappear across rural Louisiana. A new plan to hold migrants at Angola -- Louisiana's most notorious and dangerous prison. Jail time for driving someone over state lines for an abortion, ordering an abortion pill, and even for out of state doctors.
They run their tests on us, work out the kinks, and then they ship out the final product to the nation. However, decades of this abuse combined with astronomical gas prices have turned Louisiana into a powder keg that threatens to upend their cruel system and flip LA blue.
My name is Dadrius Lanus and 9 months ago I became Executive Director for the Louisiana Democratic Party. After years of ceding ground, Democrats are back on the offensive.
Just a month ago, in a special election, a Democrat in a deep red MAGA county that went for Trump by 13 points defeated a Trump endorsed Republican in a landslide 37 point over performance. It was the first win delivered by Organize Louisiana - a cutting edge new precinct organizing program to have folks on the ground who can fight in every single one of Louisiana's 4000+ precincts.
And for the first time in years we have a Democrat contesting every red federal seat this year: Conrad Cable taking on Speaker Mike Johnson in LA-04, Lauren Jewett taking on Steve Scalise in LA-01, John Day taking on Clay Higgins in LA-03, and Jessee Fleenor taking on Julia Letlow in LA-05, and Jamie Davis - our Democratic candidate running for U.S. Senate against Senator Bill Cassidy
When we compete everywhere we win. I am not being facetious when I say that if we continue to fight with this vigor, we can flip multiple red Louisiana Congressional seats along with our US Senate Seat, as well as break the GOP super majority in the Louisiana State House and Senate.

Beto will be visiting two college campuses today and tomorrow in the Rio Grande Valley to meet with students and help register them to vote.
That matters for a few reasons.
**First, the Rio Grande Valley is not easy to get to.** From El Paso, there are barely any direct flights. Making this trip takes time, planning, and resources — but if we are serious about reaching voters where they are, then we have to show up.
**Second, Texas makes voter registration harder than it should be.** There is no automatic voter registration and no online voter registration. If a student wants to vote, they often have to navigate a confusing process on their own — unless someone is there to help.
This is the kind of work that changes outcomes. It isn’t glamorous but it’s what actually moves the needle and wins elections.

body:
But then we saw the news again.

| | | | |
---
Hi Peter, There are two kinds of headlines a congressman can make. _The kind that comes from showing up in your community so often that people stop being surprised to see you._ **And the kind where the rest of the country is talking about you, and not in a good way.** Andy Ogles keeps finding his way into national headlines for all the wrong reasons. Inflammatory tweets, online rants — the kind of behavior that gets attention everywhere but is a total embarrassment to those of us here in TN-5. Meanwhile, Chaz has spent years as mayor of Columbia doing the opposite. Sitting down with folks who just need somebody to listen. Working with small business owners. Being part of the community. As I write this, voters are casting their ballots to choose which leaders will serve on the Salt River Project Board (SRP), and the outcome of this local race could have national consequences. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | AI built this rally. Paging Dan... where are you?
That's what a lot of people in our part of Pennsylvania are asking right now.
Because our congressman voted to **kick nearly 30,000 of his constituents off their health care** and has been hiding from us ever since.
I met a small business owner in Wyoming County a few weeks ago who told me about her adult son, who has special needs and relies on Medicaid for health care.
His mom is grateful for the support her son has, but she feels like their family is living on the edge. If he were kicked off Medicaid, it would wreck their life.
Dan Meuser voted to put this family, and many like them, at risk. **He voted for a historic $1 trillion Medicaid cut last year - to fund tax cuts for the very rich.** (Sounds insane, but it's real.)
If you're going to represent us, you start by showing up. You should be able to look people in the eye and explain your votes. Especially when those votes have real consequences for our lives.
But this is a pattern with Dan Meuser. He shows up for himself. He shows up for his donors. And when it comes to the people he's supposed to advocate for, he's nowhere to be found.
**I 'm running to stop health care cuts and hold insurance companies accountable. I got into this race because I couldn't sit back and watch Meuser rip a lifeline away from our neighbors.**
I'll get to work to make health care more affordable on day one, but I can't get to Congress without you.
**[Can you chip in today to help me flip this seat and fight for our part of Pennsylvania?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/bfd44cad-1873-46ca-8580-eb111a5cdb19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

We deserve better than this. Let's send someone to Congress who puts us first.
- Rachel Wallace

* * *
Donald Trump has the entire country, if not the entire world, on edge this morning with repeated threats to wipe Iran's civilization off the map. And the implication behind that rhetoric is that he's at least considering using nuclear weapons to end this illegal and disastrous war. At a bare minimum, he's already said that he's willing to strike civilian targets, which would be a pretty clear war crime.
And the truth is, I don't know how serious he is. Maybe it's just another weak man issuing threats he won't follow through on, as he's done many times before. But we've watched this president violate norm after norm, law after law. And at this point, we have to take seriously the possibility that he might do something that hasn't been done in almost 100 years: use a nuclear weapon in the middle of a war.
When it comes to Donald Trump, I tend to be somebody who takes what he says seriously. At the time that I'm writing this and sending it out, I don't know what's going to happen. The deadline is at 8 o'clock Eastern tonight. If you're reading this after, you may know more than I do about whether or not he was serious, if he backed down, or to what extent he's willing to attack the people of Iran. But I always try to take what Donald Trump says seriously so that I can better prepare for what might happen.
When he jokes about a third term, I take it seriously. When he talks about meddling in elections, I take it seriously. So when he starts talking like this, and when I see MAGA influencers like Mark Levin, who Donald Trump is very close to, start justifying and laying the groundwork for Donald Trump to use nuclear weapons, I take that very seriously.
Because what we're watching is a president who's launched an illegal war without congressional authorization, who has, by all appearances, misled the public about casualties and outcomes, and who shows a disturbing disregard for human life. People are disposable to him. He treats the world like a chess game. The only life that matters is his.
Decisions of this magnitude aren't meant to rest with one person. They're supposed to be checked, debated, and constrained. That's why we have a Constitution. And here he is, using the language of a dictator more openly than ever and, frankly, scaring the hell out of everybody.
It's not what this country is supposed to be about. This is not real leadership. We don't need reckless threats or escalating rhetoric with no clear strategy, with no clear plan to improve this situation and help the American people with their lives. What we should be doing is de-escalating. What we should be doing is leading the world and working with our allies, not alienating them. We should be understanding the weight of the decisions that are made behind the Resolute Desk. And the president of the United States, who is in control of the world's most powerful military, should act with restraint, not impulse.
At our best, America leads. We helped win World War II. We rallied the world around Ukraine. We haven't always gotten it right, but at our best, we've been a force for good--something people could look to for leadership. And in just one year, Donald Trump has shredded that credibility at home and abroad. Our allies are pushed away, our global stability has been shaken, and the economy is damaged, potentially beyond repair. The American people are scared. And when credibility erodes, the risks aren't theoretical. They get more real, more immediate, and harder to control.
Even if this nuclear threat is empty, and I suspect it is, the fact that people believe it's possible says everything about the man who sits behind the Oval Office. The fact that so many people today are calling for Donald Trump to be removed by the 25th Amendment--not just Democrats, but also core members of the MAGA movement. People like Alex Jones are starting to make sense to me on removing Donald Trump from office. Candace Owens is saying we have to remove him because he's lost his mind. It's a strange day in _paradise_ when Mike Nellis and Alex Jones and Candace Owens are all in agreement.
We are no longer dealing with hypotheticals; we're dealing with a reality people can actually see happening. We've seen what nuclear weapons can do. The only time they've ever been used in war came under extraordinary circumstances at the end of World War II--circumstances that have been debated for decades. And there will be no such justification for such action here should Donald Trump decide to do that. Multiple members of his administration have refused to rule that out, in case you think I'm being irrational.
There will not be grace. There will not be understanding. But there must be consequences if Donald Trump does something like that.

* * *
The truth is, today more than other days, I'm exhausted--and I imagine that you are too. When you think about it, we have lived through some extraordinary times: pandemics, economic instability, technological upheaval, constant political chaos. None of this is normal. People are just trying to make it through their day. They want to pay their bills. They want to find a moment's peace at night and maybe watch a basketball game. And instead, we're sitting here wondering how far this can go.
That isn't okay.
So yeah, I'm a little scared today. But what happens next matters. If things escalate--whatever he does tonight--people aren't just going to be afraid in theory. They're going to be afraid of retaliation, of what comes next, of how far this spirals. And the only way through that is together: supporting each other, staying engaged, refusing to tune out when it feels overwhelming.
Because this is one of those moments that actually matters. We don't get to look away. We don't get to assume someone else will fix it. We don't get to pretend this is normal. It's not.
And if we meet this moment with clarity, with urgency, and with a willingness to stand up for our values--for each other, for the kind of country we're supposed to be--then we'll have a chance to pull ourselves back from the brink. But that only happens if we show up.
It means paying attention, speaking out, holding leaders accountable--not letting this become background noise just because it's overwhelming and scary. And the implication behind that rhetoric is that he's at least considering using nuclear weapons to end this illegal and disastrous war. At a bare minimum, he's already said that he's willing to strike civilian targets, which would be a pretty clear war crime. And the truth is, I don't know how serious he is. Maybe it's just another weak man issuing threats he won't follow through on, as he's done many times before. But we've watched this president violate norm after norm, law after law. And at this point, we have to take seriously the possibility that he might do something that hasn't been done in almost 100 years: use a nuclear weapon in the middle of a war. When it comes to Donald Trump, I tend to be somebody who takes what he says seriously. At the time that I'm writing this and sending it out, I don't know what's going to happen. The deadline is at 8 o'clock Eastern tonight. If you're reading this after, you may know more than I do about whether or not he was serious, if he backed down, or to what extent he's willing to attack the people of Iran. But I always try to take what Donald Trump says seriously so that I can better prepare for what might happen. When he jokes about a third term, I take it seriously. When he talks about meddling in elections, I take it seriously. So when he starts talking like this, and when I see MAGA influencers like Mark Levin, who Donald Trump is very close to, start justifying and laying the groundwork for Donald Trump to use nuclear weapons, I take that very seriously. subject: Trump's executive order is illegal.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3920?t=1001&akid=1585%2E181023%2EZx5Qem ]New York Times: Trump Signs Order Seeking Federal Control of Mail
Voting as He Promotes False Claims

Let me be clear: Trump’s executive order restricting mail-in voting is
illegal.

In this country, states run our elections — not the president. That’s how
our system works, and it’s how we protect voters from exactly this kind of
political interference.

But after failing to get Congress to pass the SAVE Act, Trump is resorting
to executive action to push the same goal of making it harder for eligible
Americans to vote.

As Michigan’s Secretary of State, I’ve spent years standing up to attacks
like this, defending our elections, protecting mail-in voting, and making
sure every eligible voter can make their voice heard.

And I will continue to fight this executive order in my current role. But
if we want to stop this kind of overreach for good, we need governors who
understand the law, respect our democracy, and won’t back down, regardless
of who’s in the White House.

That’s why this race matters so much. In a battleground like Michigan,
Trump and Republicans will be looking for any way to subvert our
elections. We saw it in 2020, and now we’re seeing it again.

That’s why I need your help to keep this governor’s office blue. We need
the resources to fight back against these attacks, reach voters with the
truth, and build a campaign strong enough to win.

Peter,

President Donald Trump, with the most powerful military on Earth at his command, just sent out an unhinged tweet threatening Iran — claiming “a whole civilization will die tonight” if he doesn’t get his way.

Trump’s illegal war in Iran has already led to enormous death and destruction, including a school bombing that killed over 100 children. We cannot allow him to set fire to the world.
I was proud to speak out against this war from the very beginning and stand up as a strong yes vote on a War Powers Resolution — proud to do my job and vote to force him to stop. But Republicans blocked us, proving that they’re committed to enabling him every step of the way.
I’m committed to stopping this illegal, unconstitutional war. And I’m not going to stop standing up and speaking out until Congress acts to end it.

I watched my parents pour themselves into their work. My dad believed deeply in building communities where people could thrive. My mom believed just as deeply that every voice — especially women's voices — deserved to be heard. I was proud of both of them.

But politics? I thought it was too competitive. Too brutal. Too much.

But when I became a mom to a son with cerebral palsy, I found myself getting involved as an advocate for kids with disabilities. I made it all the way to the Governor’s office.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128998858/612949537/1146729020?amount=5&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.04.07_Never-Run-For-Office_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4Nzg5MWNkNC1jNjMyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jFO3UnypmYnMuozQ635NLHEjfJq-1mjvwSbOn-LL7tE=)
Then, the same night that Donald Trump won the presidency for the first time, I won my U.S. Senate seat by just 1,017 votes.

That narrow margin taught me something I've carried ever since: Every single vote matters. Every dollar raised matters. Every door knocked, every conversation had — it all matters.

And when Democrats win, we get to work. **In the Senate, I've fought alongside my colleagues to deliver real results for hardworking families:**
* Capped the cost of insulin at $35/month for Medicare recipients
* Secured billions in funding for veterans' health care and toxic exposure benefits
* Helped pass the biggest investment in American infrastructure in a generation
* Fought to lower prescription drug costs and protect Social Security and Medicare
* Stood up for reproductive rights and the freedom to control our own futures

This is what democracy can do. It's not just an idea — it’s about real people's lives: the veteran who finally gets the care that he was promised, the grandmother who can afford her medication, the bridge that gets repaired so families can get where they're going safely.

To Donald Trump and his allies, 2024 was only the beginning

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128998892/612949629/-1368017556?amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&refcode=email_040726_standingintrumpsway&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzE2MjYzZS1jNzMyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wJMRRKwuENiCt7NSpNj2Gr7jYDDeWbUfsernpprsLVw=) Derek, Donald Trump won 31 states in the last Presidential election — including Pennsylvania. Of those states, seven were represented by a Democratic Governor. **And in this election?
